successors.name: Danish Estonia
successors.text: Revelia, Harrien, Vironia and Jerwia: the whole of northern Estonia

successors.name: Livonian Brothers of the Sword
successors.text: southern Estonia, Rotalia and Saaremaa; the Bishoprics of Dorpat and Ösel-Wiek took part of it

ledger.x: 1208: the crusaders open operations against the Estonians.
1208: raids on Sakala and Ugaunia begin.
1220: the rest of northern Estonia is Danish.
1224: the contest for Sakala and Ugaunia ends with the fall of Tartu (the Brothers of the Sword dossier ends its Sakala-Ugandi contest in 1227).
August 1224: Tartu falls and the south is lost.
1227: Saaremaa falls and the last Estonian lands with it.

1227: the last free Estonian land is conquered; the ecclesiastical state Terra Mariana is established and the territory is divided among the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order, the Bishopric of Dorpat and the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek, while the north stays a nominal Danish possession until 1346.

wars.name: Estonian Crusade
wars.outcome: The Estonians lost northern Estonia to the Danes (1219-1220), Sakala and Ugaunia to the Brothers of the Sword and the Bishop of Dorpat (Tartu, August 1224) and Saaremaa in 1227; the Treaty of Stensby of 7 June 1238 returned the Duchy of Estonia to Valdemar II.

certainty.note: Counties without boundaries; the page names eight major and seven smaller counties and locates only Saaremaa, Harjumaa and Rävala.
